subject: maths
question: An article is sold for Rs. 54120 after two successive discounts of 12 percent and 18 percent. What is the marked price of the article ?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier after 12% and 18% discounts = 0.88 × 0.82 = 0.7216.

Marked Price (MP) × Net multiplier = Selling Price (SP).

MP × 0.7216 = 54120.

MP = 54120 ÷ 0.7216 = 75000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 75000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 54120

First Discount (D₁) = 12%

Second Discount (D₂) = 18%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/136c4f65b2300d91ccccc3bb20a5ec5f50364b64d026919c9e3bccc1ff68ad91.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54120 = MP × (100 − 12)/100 × (100 − 18)/100

⇒ 54120 = MP × (88/100) × (82/100)

⇒ 54120 = MP × 0.88 × 0.82

⇒ 54120 = MP × 0.7216

⇒ MP = 54120 ÷ 0.7216

⇒ MP = 75000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 75000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

The effective discount for two successive discounts x% and y% is given by the formula: Effective Discount = [x + y − (x × y)/100]%.

Relationship between MP and SP

Marked Price is the price printed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP: SP = MP − Discount or SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up = Marked Price − Cost Price. Mark-up % = [(MP − CP)/CP] × 100.</p
